vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: The advisory and b81a3fc fix identify stored line-item HTML and replace the input denylist with Purify::clean(), but the primary does not close an executable sink in the affected release. At v5.13.3, resources/views/portal/ninja2020/components/html-viewer.blade.php applies Purify::clean() to both product and service notes, and PdfService::getHtml() applies Purify::clean() to both JSON-design HTML and the generated document. The default DISABLE_PURIFY_HTML value is false. A reachable unpurified sink or a bypass of these output sanitizers was not demonstrated.

atomic_bic.evidence: 192722b7a47556bef14e0460df25d71ee570a73a first adds str_replace("</", "<-") to notes/product_key, but its parent already accepts the same report payloads without any line-item filter. This change is a partial mitigation, not the commit that first changed a safe parent into the vulnerable state. The earlier 1c9450a6e4eac9b90aacc70ec6ef1f010681e904 raw-HTML portal change was itself mitigated by e9493d597b8311f9e7855d5b8b93ec399536cfea before v5.13.0, so it also does not by itself close the advisory's affected-release mechanism.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: The tree of parent 2c253710111b9189524e273e8416650088fec425 lacks the denylist lines, but absence of a mitigation is not absence of the vulnerability: report payloads pass through unchanged. The required non-vulnerable-parent transition for 192722b7 was therefore not proven.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: 192722b7 is a single-parent public commit and an individual member of PR 9291; it is not the PR merge aggregate a72058525e4c934a2c7bc443ad13aef2a871a7da. No further squash decomposition is needed for that candidate.

affected_release_membership.evidence: 192722b7 is an ancestor of peeled tags v5.13.0 (936ff9cf3326b2774bc8dc0aa8fa1eca11ce5b20) and v5.13.3 (6d3480fc09174971528111a69859ae644c052799); CVE-2026-33628 is PUBLISHED and records versions < 5.13.4 as affected. This establishes release membership, not the missing executable path or BIC.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: b81a3fc302573fc4a53d61e8537dd19154ce1091 is not an ancestor of v5.13.3 and is an ancestor of peeled tag v5.13.4 (5ff2095eafe4a891807e4be7a91e1bfb8e56269c).

direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched_state.evidence: The advisory cites b81a3fc302573fc4a53d61e8537dd19154ce1091. Its CleanLineItems hunk replaces the four-token denylist with Purify::clean($item[$field], true), and its new tests exercise the stated denylist-bypass payloads; fdcec3a4eb180c09d1760e89962874c4289cfee8 immediately removes the temporary character guard and logging while retaining Purify.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The primary checks AI markers only on 192722b7, whose commit object and PR member metadata identify turbo124/David Bomba and contain no AI trailers. Because 192722b7 is not a proven causal BIC, those facts cannot support NOT_AI for the vulnerability. AI attribution must remain unresolved until the actual atomic introducer is established.

findings: The primary simultaneously acknowledges output purification in the affected release and asserts execution in those same portal/PDF sinks without proving a sanitizer bypass.
The proposed introducer adds an incomplete defense to an already-unfiltered parent; it does not satisfy the protocol definition of the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable behavior.
Consequently the BIC-only AI gate is open, so NOT_AI is not claim-grade even though the proposed candidate has human account metadata and no visible AI marker.

corrected_fields.bug_semantics: Stored line-item HTML is confirmed to bypass the historical input denylist and b81a3fc is a relevant hardening fix, but execution through an affected-release unpurified sink or a bypass of the existing portal/PDF Purify calls remains unproven.

remaining_gap: Identify and reproduce a reachable unpurified source-to-sink path (or a concrete bypass of Purify::clean()) in an affected tag, then trace the first public commit that changes its immediate parent from non-vulnerable to vulnerable and inspect AI provenance on that actual BIC only.
